t: You're looking at numbers 19, 20 and 21, together with their walls, gate piers and former lodge, in Camden. They were designed by Horace Field, a London-born architect who lived from 1861 to 1948. Field often worked in a Wrenaissance style, drawing on the Arts and Crafts movement and on Richard Norman Shaw. He designed large houses and offices, including a number of works for Lloyds Bank and offices for the North Eastern Railway in London and York. Here, you're seeing his house design, complete with its boundary details.
